title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Grothendieck is in the 'équation des lacets' part of the Longue Marche continuation. The objects are as follows.
- pi_{0,3}^ is the profinite fundamental group of P^1 - {0,1,inf}. It is free profinite on loops l_0 and l_1, around 0 and 1.
- G^+_{0,3} is a profinite group containing it, the fundamental group of an orbifold quotient. In it there are elements eps_0 and eps_1 with eps_0^2 = l_0 and eps_1^2 = l_1, and an involution sigma_inf exchanging 0 and 1, with sigma_inf(eps_1) = eps_0.
- M^{!~}_{0,3} is a group of 'loop' automorphisms of G^+_{0,3} stabilising pi_{0,3}^. N^{!~}_{0,3} is its image in outer automorphisms, which contains Gamma_Q = Gal(Qbar/Q).
- M^{!}_{0,3} is the extension of Gamma_Q by pi_{0,3}^ coming from the Galois action.

Previous page. Automorphisms normalising L_0 (the inertia subgroup at 0) and satisfying the normalisation hat-phi(f) = f must be of the form u_xi = u_{(alpha,beta,1)}, where xi = alpha rho(alpha)^{-1} and xi solves (14),(15). Corollary 4 says these form a subgroup M^{!≈}_{0,3}(omega). This subgroup meets pi_{0,3}^ (the inner automorphisms) trivially and maps isomorphically onto N^{!≈}_{0,3}, the outer loop automorphisms whose hat-phi commutes exterieurement with u.

This page proves the remaining claim: u_xi is inner only if xi = 1.
1. By the proposition of p.404, u_{alpha,beta,1} is inner iff alpha and beta are powers l_0^n, with n in Z^. Then xi = l_0^n l_1^{-n} and eta = beta sigma_inf(beta)^{-1} = l_0^n l_1^{-n}.
2. The relation xi = eta l_1^nu then forces l_1^nu = 1, so nu = 0.
3. Relation (15) becomes l_0^n l_1^{-n} = eps_0^n (sigma eps_1^n sigma).
4. Using l_i = eps_i^2 and sigma eps_1^n sigma = eps_0^n, this gives eps_0^{2n} eps_1^{-2n} = eps_0^{2n}. Hence eps_1^{2n} = l_1^n = 1, so n = 0 because l_1 generates a free Z^. So xi = 1.

Consequence. There is a canonical partial section of M^{!~}_{0,3} -> N^{!~}_{0,3} over N^{!≈}_{0,3}. Since N^{!≈}_{0,3} contains Gamma_Q (next page), this restricts to a canonical splitting of 1 -> pi_{0,3}^ -> M^!_{0,3} -> Gamma_Q -> 1, landing in the normaliser of the inertia L_0. This is the profinite-group-theoretic construction of a Galois-equivariant 'base point at 0'.

Next page. Grothendieck asks whether this section corresponds to a tangential base point, i.e. a uniformiser at 0 modulo m_0^2. He proposes the Z-integral generators +-z and asks which sign is right: 'Mais est-ce bien le bon? Il faudrait y revenir!'
errors: A first attempted simplification writes eps_0^n = eps_1^{3n} ('d'où n=0'). This does not follow from the relation, and Grothendieck abandons it for the correct simplification just below.
The final 'i.e. comme n=0' is slightly circular in wording: n = 0 should be the conclusion drawn from eps_1^{2n} = l_1^n = 1, which in turn gives xi = 1.

The written relation shows 'sigma_inf^n' factors. Since sigma_inf is an involution, the intended expression is the conjugate sigma_inf eps_1^n sigma_inf, as the underbrace confirms. This is a notational slip or transcription ambiguity, not a mathematical error.
Whether beta should be l_0^n or a power of l_1 depends on conventions on p.404 that are not visible here; consistency with eta = l_0^n l_1^{-n} suggests beta = l_0^n with sigma_inf(l_0) = l_1.

ideas.what: Criterion for when a normalised loop automorphism u_xi is inner (xi = 1), giving trivial intersection with pi^ and an isomorphism of M^{!≈} onto N^{!≈}
ideas.modern_name: Injectivity / splitting step in a Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type normalisation (pairs (lambda,f) with f normalised)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara (1990s) for GT^ and its normalisations

ideas.what: Canonical Galois-equivariant splitting of 1 -> pi_1^(P^1-{0,1,inf}) -> Ext -> Gamma_Q -> 1, inside the normaliser of the inertia at 0
ideas.modern_name: Tangential base point at 0 (e.g. the vector 01->), i.e. a Galois section attached to a cusp/inertia subgroup
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (1989, 'Le groupe fondamental de la droite projective moins trois points'), Ihara, Anderson; cuspidal sections in anabelian geometry (Nakamura et al.)
ideas.where_published: Possibly alluded to in La Longue Marche (1981) or the Esquisse (base points 'at infinity'); unsure

ideas.what: Question of identifying the section with a choice of uniformiser in m_0/m_0^2, normalised over Z up to sign (z or -z)
ideas.modern_name: Dependence of tangential base points on the tangent vector; integral normalisation of tangential base points

missed.claim: Grothendieck constructs, purely group-theoretically (from the loop equation with the extra order-2 symmetry sigma_inf and the square roots eps_i of the inertia generators), a canonical Galois section normalising L_0. He then leaves open which tangent vector, z or -z, it corresponds to.
missed.quote: on a donc trouvé une section partielle canonique de M_{0,3}^{!~} au dessus des sous-groupes N_{0,3}^{!≈} de N_{0,3}^{!~}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is an independent pre-Deligne route to tangential base points via an orbifold extension G^+ in which l_0 has a square root. The sign question (z vs -z) is tied to the half-loops eps_i, which relates to known subtleties of the 01-> versus 10-> paths and of 2-torsion in GT. Settling it would confirm historical priority and fix conventions. Most of this content is, however, now standard.

deep.surprise_reason: The computation itself is routine. The interest is historical: Grothendieck independently derives a canonical Galois section at the cusp 0 from the loop-equation formalism, and explicitly asks whether it equals the tangential base point given by z or -z, i.e. Deligne's tangential base points avant la lettre. This is suggestive but largely subsumed by Deligne/Ihara.
transcription_corrections: 'ε_1^{2n} = 0' in the image should be read as meaning '= 1'.
The factors 'σ_∞^n' are likely 'σ_∞' (conjugation by the involution), as the underbrace σ_∞(ε_1)^n = ε_0^n indicates.
Page number at the top is 419 (the notes' own pagination); 236 at the bottom is the archive page number.

The left-margin oblique note is largely illegible; it seems to read 'NB X_{0,3}^{!~} = Γ_{0,3}^{!~} ... de M_{0,3}^{!~} ... \bar N_{0,3}^{!~} était ... (mais !) Définir variante partielle ... renforcement'.
